classification.difficultyReason: Construct the triangle of centres, derive its angles and subtract three sectors to obtain the central gap.

content.prompt: Three circles are tangent to each other as shown in the diagram below. Two of the circles have radii of 6, and the smaller circle has a radius of 4. Find the area bounded by these three circles.

spec.description: Two equal lower circles and one smaller upper circle, all externally tangent. Decorative source fills are omitted; the central curvilinear gap remains identifiable.
spec.mathematics: Lower radii are 6 and upper radius is 4. Centres at (-6,0), (6,0) and (0,8) give centre distances 12, 10 and 10, exactly the sums of the corresponding radii.
spec.answerVisibility: No construction lines, centre labels, angles or answers appear in the question diagram.

answer.short:
$48-8\pi-20\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac43\right)$ square units, with the inverse tangent evaluated in radians.

Subtract the three sectors from the triangle formed by the circle centres.
answer.worked:
Join the three centres. Their triangle has side lengths $10$, $10$ and $12$. Let its height be $h$ and each base angle be $\alpha$, measured in radians.

$$\begin{align*}h&=\sqrt{10^2-6^2}\\h&=8\\\alpha&=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac86\right)\\\alpha&=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac43\right).\end{align*}$$

The angle at the upper centre is $\pi-2\alpha$. The required gap is the triangle minus the three sectors.

$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12(12)(8)-2\left(\frac12\cdot6^2\alpha\right)-\frac12\cdot4^2(\pi-2\alpha)\\A&=48-36\alpha-8\pi+16\alpha\\A&=48-8\pi-20\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac43\right)\text{ square units}.\end{align*}$$
